title: Module impact graph linter + contextual policy enforcer for VPC IaC
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: As we scale Private (VPC) deployments we see two recurring risks in Terraform changes: 1) blind plan/apply that obscures resource-level blast radius when modules touch many accounts or shared networking components, and 2) policy checks that operate only on the flat plan JSON without considering module graph context (ordering, implicit dependencies, maintenance windows).

Objective: Deliver a CI-stage pipeline component that performs (A) a static Terraform module dependency/impact graph analysis and resource blast-radius scoring, (B) a contextual policy evaluation step that enriches Conftest/OPA checks with graph metadata (module owner, resource tier, maintenance windows), and (C) automated safe-apply guidance (staged apply groups) plus post-apply active health checks with automatic rollback hooks.

Deliverables:
- A CLI library (golang) that consumes terraform plan JSON and produces a resource impact graph + blast-radius score per resource and per module.
- A policy adapter that converts the graph and plan into a richer evaluation context for Conftest/OPA (labels: module_owner, business_tier, modifies_public_subnet, cross_account_change).
- A CI pipeline step (CircleCI/GitHub Actions compatible) that: lint -> graph analysis -> policy evaluation -> cost delta estimation -> staged-apply plan generation suggestion.
- Post-apply health-check hooks: automated TCP/ICMP path tests between affected endpoints, route table validation, and smoke check probes for endpoint reachability. Failures trigger automated rollback with runnable apply plan for revert.
- Documentation and runbook for on-call and SRE owners.

Acceptance criteria:
- The linter produces a human-readable graph visualization and a JSON artifact showing per-resource impact and a total blast-radius score.
- Policies can reference graph attributes in Conftest rego tests; at least three example policies included (no-public-ip-on-core-subnet, maintenance-window-required-for-db-mods, cross-account-change-allowed-for-admins-only).
- CI step blocks PRs with policy failures and attaches remediation hints (which module to split, suggested maintenance window, or recommended staging groups).
- Post-apply health checks run as part of an optional staged-apply and can automatically run the rollback apply plan if smoke checks fail within 15 minutes.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We intentionally keep the static analysis conservative: over-approximate edges where Terraform uses data-driven references to avoid unsafe applies. That increases false positives but reduces risk.
- Using Conftest/OPA as the primary policy engine allows us to reuse existing policies, but we add a small adapter layer (no policy engine fork) to inject graph metadata. This keeps policies declarative and testable.
- Staged apply is opt-in per repo via a .redwood-ci.yaml flag so existing infra teams can opt-in without breaking current flows.
- We avoid building a full planner that executes partial applies: instead we synthesize grouped plans and rely on Terraform apply workspaces and targeted applies to execute groups. This limits complexity while enabling safe rollouts.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Prototype graph extractor (week 1-2): parse plan JSON, map resources to modules, compute dependency graph and rudimentary blast radius metrics (resource type criticality, number of consumers).
2) Policy adapter (week 3): define graph schema and wire up an adapter that outputs policy context JSON consumed by Conftest tests.
3) CI step + runner scripts (week 4): build Action/Orb that runs linter + policy + cost delta. Provide human-readable HTML report and a machine JSON artifact.
4) Post-apply hooks (week 5): add a suite of probe scripts (python) that can run from a bastion or ephemeral runner to validate network paths and endpoints specified by module metadata.
5) Rollout & docs (week 6): soft rollout to infra-team, gather feedback, iterate on false positives and policy tuning.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for graph extractor with synthetic plans (multi-module scenarios, cross-account, shared-subnet cases).
- Integration tests in a sandbox account using small module changes that touch routing and SGs; validate staged apply + rollback flows.
- Load test the CI step on a repo with 200-module mono-repo to ensure performance targets (<=30s for linter on typical plan sizes).

Monitoring and metrics:
- Policy violation rate per repo and per policy ID.
- Average blast-radius score for merged changes over time.
- Post-apply failure rate and rollback frequency.
- Alerts: >3 rollbacks within 24h triggers an on-call page to infra and SRE.

Risks & mitigations:
- False positives causing developer friction: start conservative, ship an "analysis-only" mode and iterate policy thresholds; provide clear bypass instructions with required approvals.
- Post-apply rollback complexity: keep rollback plan generation deterministic and attach to the original PR so operators can re-run manually.
- Secrets/credentials for post-apply probes: use ephemeral short-lived runner tokens and customer-managed KMS keys for target account probes.

Runbook excerpt (brief):
- On merge with staged-apply enabled: CI will create group-apply plans and notify owners in PR with the HTML report.
- If post-apply smoke checks fail: the pipeline triggers a rollback apply automatically and posts a summary in the PR with probe logs and stackdriver links.
- If rollback fails, page SRE and include the revert plan link.

Acceptance test links and references:
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/73529102/Module+Impact+Graph+Linter
- Prototype PR (infra repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/6123
- Example Conftest policies and samples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/main/ci/policies/module-graph
- Cost estimator service docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/cost-estimator

Notes: This ticket intentionally covers the analysis and CI-enforcement surface; a follow-up ticket will add an operator UI in the Console for interactive staged applies and one-click rollbacks.
